title: Can we improve our memory
paragraphs: We've all been there – staring at a pile of books, desperately hoping that what we study will stick in our mind. Many of us have probably asked if there's any way that we can get better at remembering things. So, why don't we look at what memory experts say about this?

Every student who has made flashcards knows that it can be helpful to go back over what they've studied before. According to The Learning Scientists – a group of cognitive scientists – we can learn things better if we wait for some time before trying to study them again. They say that trying to retrieve something from your memory after you have had some time to forget it will make it easier to remember in future.

Similarly, David Robson, writing for BBC Future, highlights studies that show taking some time to just do nothing after studying might mean that you can remember things better afterwards. We don't know exactly why this happens, but it has been suggested that it's to do with the relationship between long-term and short-term memory.

Another study tip from The Learning Scientists is to change between different topics as you study. They say this can help you build links between different ideas. Now, linking ideas and relating them to each other or to images are often suggested as good ways to memorise something. Former world memory champion Jonathan Hancock highlights how picturing pieces of information in different physical locations or linking them to memorable images makes them easier to remember.

Linking new information to things that are easier to remember is a technique that many people use – it could be making letter patterns into words called mnemonics, or by sorting things into categories.

There are also more general things that we can do to improve our memory. Hancock says that being generally organised makes things easier for your brain, while many other experts also recommend avoiding stress, alcohol and smoking, and that we should get a lot of rest and exercise. So, the good news to take from this is that while it may be hard, improving our memory is something we can control.

vocabulary.entry: stick in one's mind /stɪk ɪn wʌnz maɪnd/  铭记；牢记；留在脑海中
vocabulary.example: That unforgettable moment will stick in my mind forever.
vocabulary.translation: 那个难忘的瞬间会永远留在我的脑海里。

vocabulary.entry: flashcard /ˈflæʃkɑːd/ n. 抽认卡；记忆卡片
vocabulary.example: She made flashcards to memorize the new English words.
vocabulary.translation: 她做了抽认卡来记忆新的英语单词。

vocabulary.entry: go back over /ɡəʊ bæk ˈəʊvə/  重温；重新查阅；回顾
vocabulary.example: I need to go back over the lecture notes before the final exam.
vocabulary.translation: 期末考试前我需要重温一下课堂笔记。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive /ˈkɒɡnətɪv/ adj. 认知的；与认识能力相关的
vocabulary.example: The study focuses on children's cognitive development in early childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究聚焦于儿童幼儿时期的认知发展。

vocabulary.entry: retrieve /rɪˈtriːv/ v. 回忆起；检索；找回
vocabulary.example: It's difficult to retrieve the exact details of the event after so many years.
vocabulary.translation: 这么多年过去，很难回忆起这件事的具体细节。

vocabulary.entry: long-term memory /ˌlɒŋ tɜːm ˈmeməri/ n. 长期记忆
vocabulary.example: Long-term memory enables us to store information for years or even a lifetime.
vocabulary.translation: 长期记忆让我们能将信息储存数年甚至一生。

vocabulary.entry: short-term memory /ˌʃɔːt tɜːm ˈmeməri/ n. 短期记忆
vocabulary.example: Short-term memory can only hold a small amount of information for a short while.
vocabulary.translation: 短期记忆只能在短时间内储存少量信息。

vocabulary.entry: build links /bɪld lɪŋks/  建立联系；构建关联
vocabulary.example: We should build links between different knowledge points when studying.
vocabulary.translation: 学习时我们应该在不同的知识点之间建立联系。

vocabulary.entry: memorise /ˈmeməraɪz/ v. 熟记；记住；记忆
vocabulary.example: He can memorise a whole page of English text in just five minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 他能在短短五分钟内熟记一整页的英语课文。

vocabulary.entry: champion /ˈtʃæmpiən/ n. 冠军；优胜者；拥护者
vocabulary.example: He won the title of world memory champion at the age of 25.
vocabulary.translation: 他25岁时获得了世界记忆冠军的称号。

vocabulary.entry: picture /ˈpɪktʃə(r)/ v. 想象；描绘；构想
vocabulary.example: I can picture the beautiful scenery of the mountain village clearly.
vocabulary.translation: 我能清晰地想象出那个山村的美丽景色。

vocabulary.entry: physical location /ˈfɪzɪkl ləʊˈkeɪʃn/ n. 实际位置；具体场所
vocabulary.example: The app can help you find the physical location of the nearest bookstore.
vocabulary.translation: 这个应用能帮你找到最近书店的具体场所。

vocabulary.entry: memorable /ˈmemərəbl/ adj. 难忘的；值得纪念的；印象深刻的
vocabulary.example: We had a memorable trip to the coast during the summer holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 暑假我们去海边度过了一次难忘的旅行。

vocabulary.entry: technique /tekˈniːk/ n. 技巧；方法；技术
vocabulary.example: This memorisation technique is widely used by language learners.
vocabulary.translation: 这种记忆技巧被语言学习者广泛运用。

vocabulary.entry: pattern /ˈpætn/ n. 模式；图案；规律
vocabulary.example: We can find a clear pattern in the way he arranges the words.
vocabulary.translation: 在他的用词排列方式中我们能发现清晰的规律。

vocabulary.entry: mnemonic /nɪˈmɒnɪk/ n. 记忆术；助记符 adj. 助记的
vocabulary.example: Many students use a mnemonic to remember the colors of the rainbow.
vocabulary.translation: 很多学生用一种记忆术来记住彩虹的颜色。

vocabulary.entry: sort into /sɔːt ˈɪntuː/  把……分类；整理成
vocabulary.example: She began to sort the books into different categories by genre.
vocabulary.translation: 她开始把书籍按体裁分成不同的类别。

vocabulary.entry: category /ˈkætəɡəri/ n. 类别；种类；范畴
vocabulary.example: These artworks fall into the same category of modern painting.
vocabulary.translation: 这些艺术品都属于现代绘画的同一类别。

vocabulary.entry: organised /ˈɔːɡənaɪzd/ adj. 有条理的；有组织的；安排有序的
vocabulary.example: An organised study plan can improve your learning efficiency greatly.
vocabulary.translation: 一份有条理的学习计划能大幅提升你的学习效率。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive scientist /ˈkɒɡnətɪv ˈsaɪəntɪst/ n. 认知科学家
vocabulary.example: The cognitive scientist is conducting research on human memory ability.
vocabulary.translation: 这位认知科学家正在开展关于人类记忆能力的研究。

vocabulary.entry: memory expert /ˈmeməri ˈekspɜːt/ n. 记忆专家
vocabulary.example: The memory expert shared some useful tips for improving memory.
vocabulary.translation: 这位记忆专家分享了一些提升记忆力的实用技巧。

vocabulary.entry: study tip /ˈstʌdi tɪp/ n. 学习技巧；学习小贴士
vocabulary.example: This simple study tip helps you remember what you've learned better.
vocabulary.translation: 这个简单的学习技巧能帮你更好地记住所学的内容。

vocabulary.entry: letter pattern /ˈletə ˈpætn/ n. 字母组合模式；字母排列规律
vocabulary.example: We can use a letter pattern to create a mnemonic for vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以利用字母组合模式为词汇创造助记符。

vocabulary.entry: world memory champion /wɜːld ˈmeməri ˈtʃæmpiən/ n. 世界记忆冠军
vocabulary.example: The world memory champion can recall hundreds of numbers in order.
vocabulary.translation: 这位世界记忆冠军能按顺序记住数百个数字。

vocabulary.entry: information retrieval /ˌɪnfəˈmeɪʃn rɪˈtriːvl/ n. 信息提取；记忆检索
vocabulary.example: Information retrieval is a key part of the human memory process.
vocabulary.translation: 信息提取是人类记忆过程中的关键环节。

vocabulary.entry: mental organisation /ˈmentl ˌɔːɡənaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 心理条理；思维整理
vocabulary.example: Good mental organisation can help improve your memory retention.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的思维整理能帮助提升你的记忆留存率。

vocabulary.entry: memory retention /ˈmeməri rɪˈtenʃn/ n. 记忆留存；记忆保持能力
vocabulary.example: Regular review is an effective way to enhance memory retention.
vocabulary.translation: 定期复习是提升记忆留存能力的有效方法。

sentences.english: We've all been there – staring at a pile of books, desperately hoping that what we study will stick in our mind.
sentences.chinese: 我们都有过这样的经历——盯着一堆书，迫切地希望自己学的内容能牢牢记在脑子里。

sentences.english: Many of us have probably asked if there's any way that we can get better at remembering things.
sentences.chinese: 很多人可能都问过，有没有什么方法能让我们的记忆力变得更好？

sentences.english: So, why don't we look at what memory experts say about this?
sentences.chinese: 那么，我们不妨来看看记忆专家是怎么说的。

sentences.english: Every student who has made flashcards knows that it can be helpful to go back over what they've studied before.
sentences.chinese: 每个做过抽认卡的学生都知道，复习之前学过的内容是很有帮助的。

sentences.english: According to The Learning Scientists – a group of cognitive scientists – we can learn things better if we wait for some time before trying to study them again.
sentences.chinese: 认知科学家团队“学习科学家”指出，如果我们间隔一段时间再去复习所学内容，学习效果会更好。

sentences.english: They say that trying to retrieve something from your memory after you have had some time to forget it will make it easier to remember in future.
sentences.chinese: 他们表示，在经过一段时间、有些内容快要遗忘时，尝试从记忆中提取这些信息，会让它们在未来更容易被记起。

sentences.english: Similarly, David Robson, writing for BBC Future, highlights studies that show taking some time to just do nothing after studying might mean that you can remember things better afterwards.
sentences.chinese: 无独有偶，为BBC未来频道撰稿的大卫·罗布森强调，有研究表明，学习后花点时间什么都不做，可能会让你之后的记忆力变得更好。

sentences.english: We don't know exactly why this happens, but it has been suggested that it's to do with the relationship between long-term and short-term memory.
sentences.chinese: 我们目前还不完全清楚背后的原因，但有观点认为，这与长时记忆和短时记忆之间的关联有关。

sentences.english: Another study tip from The Learning Scientists is to change between different topics as you study.
sentences.chinese: “学习科学家”团队还给出了另一个学习技巧：学习时穿插不同的主题。

sentences.english: They say this can help you build links between different ideas.
sentences.chinese: 他们认为，这样做有助于在不同的知识点之间建立联系。

sentences.english: Now, linking ideas and relating them to each other or to images are often suggested as good ways to memorise something.
sentences.chinese: 而将知识点相互关联，或是把它们和具体图像联系起来，向来都被视为有效的记忆方法。

sentences.english: Former world memory champion Jonathan Hancock highlights how picturing pieces of information in different physical locations or linking them to memorable images makes them easier to remember.
sentences.chinese: 前世界记忆冠军乔纳森·汉考克强调，把信息片段想象成储存在不同的具体位置，或是将其与容易记住的图像绑定，都能让记忆变得更轻松。

sentences.english: Linking new information to things that are easier to remember is a technique that many people use – it could be making letter patterns into words called mnemonics, or by sorting things into categories.
sentences.chinese: 将新信息与更容易记住的事物关联起来，是很多人都会用的技巧——比如把字母组合转化成单词的记忆术，或是将信息分门别类。

sentences.english: There are also more general things that we can do to improve our memory.
sentences.chinese: 此外，还有一些更通用的方法可以提升记忆力。

sentences.english: Hancock says that being generally organised makes things easier for your brain, while many other experts also recommend avoiding stress, alcohol and smoking, and that we should get a lot of rest and exercise.
sentences.chinese: 汉考克表示，保持生活条理清晰，能让大脑的运转更轻松。其他许多专家也建议，要避免压力过大，远离酒精和烟草，同时保证充足的休息和适量的运动。

sentences.english: So, the good news to take from this is that while it may be hard, improving our memory is something we can control.
sentences.chinese: 所以，我们可以从中得到一个好消息：提升记忆力虽然并非易事，但它是一件我们能够掌控的事情。
